findings.issue_text: Backup-code login never sends the code to the server: `backupCode` is registered via `methods.register("backupCode")` in the BackupCode component but is never added to the login form's zod `formSchema`, so `zodResolver` strips it from the parsed values passed to `signIn("credentials", …)`, leaving `credentials.backupCode` always `undefined` server-side.

As a consequence of the missing schema field, a user who lost their authenticator enters a valid backup code and submits, but the request goes out without `backupCode`, `authorize()` falls into the TOTP branch, sees an empty `totpCode`, and throws `SecondFactorRequired`; the client handler for that error just re-sets `twoFactorRequired(true)` — a no-op — so nothing visibly happens (no error, no login), the user remains locked out with zero feedback, and the new `IncorrectBackupCode`/`MissingBackupCodes` handlers in `handleSignInError` are unreachable.

Existing 2FA users can never have backup codes: the `backupCodes` column is new, so every user who enabled 2FA before this deploy has `backupCodes = null` while `twoFactorEnabled = true`, and backup codes are only generated in `setup.ts`, which is only reachable through the enable modal (i.e., only when 2FA is disabled); there is no regenerate/manage-codes UI.

The `MissingBackupCodes` error message ("No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings.") actively misleads pre-existing 2FA users: generating codes is impossible without first disabling 2FA, which requires the TOTP code the user may have just lost, making "Lost access" a dead end for exactly the population most likely to need it.

`onEnable()` in `EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx` is deferred to the "Close" button instead of firing immediately on a 200 from the enable API, so closing the modal via X, ESC, or outside-click bypasses it, leaving parent state stale and enabling a code-overwrite path.

Backup-code login is non-functional: the `backupCode` field is never transmitted to the server because the `signIn("credentials", { ... })` call and the zod `formSchema` passed to `zodResolver` are unchanged in the diff, and zod strips unknown keys by default — so `credentials.backupCode` is always undefined, the server falls into the TOTP branch and returns `SecondFactorRequired`, trapping users in a login loop and making the new `IncorrectBackupCode`/`MissingBackupCodes` error handling unreachable dead code

A valid backup code is consumed (nulled and persisted) inside `authorize()` before the session is actually issued, so if anything fails later in the sign-in pipeline or the response/cookie is lost in transit, the code is permanently burned with no access granted

The backup-code consumption (read-decrypt-null-write) is not atomic/transactional, so two concurrent requests presenting the same code can both read the original array and both succeed, violating the single-use guarantee the UI explicitly promises

Existing 2FA users can never obtain backup codes: codes are generated only in `setup.ts` during the enable flow, with no backfill migration, regenerate endpoint, or settings UI, so users who enabled 2FA before this PR have `backupCodes: NULL` permanently and the `missing_backup_codes` error message directs them to 'generate them in your settings' — an action that does not exist anywhere in the product

`onEnable()` never fires when the backup-codes dialog is dismissed via the X button, Escape, or `onOpenChange(false)` at the `DisplayBackupCodes` step, leaving the settings 2FA toggle showing 'off' after 2FA was actually enabled and leaving internal state (`step`, `backupCodes`, `dataUri`) stale for the next open

EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx: object URL and sensitive state are never released on modal close/unmount — resetState() never calls URL.revokeObjectURL and never clears backupCodes, backupCodesUrl, dataUri, or secret; there is no unmount useEffect cleanup, and resetState is not wired to the Dialog's onOpenChange (so ESC/overlay close skips it entirely), leaking a Blob/object URL per setup run and leaving plaintext backup codes and the TOTP secret lingering in state with a stale step on reopen

next-auth-options.ts:139-156: backup-code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write — decrypt/parse, match, null in memory, then a separate unconditional prisma.user.update with no transaction, optimistic-concurrency check, or row locking — so two concurrent sign-ins presenting the same valid code both read the pre-update value, both pass, and both get sessions, breaking the single-use guarantee

next-auth-options.ts: the backup code is burned (persisted as consumed) before the session is actually issued, so any later failure in the sign-in flow permanently wastes a code the user can never recover

apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts:58,61 (same shape at next-auth-options.ts:139-144): JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...)) runs with no try/catch and req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "") assumes a string, so a non-string backupCode or corrupt/mismatched-key stored data throws unhandled 500s on an auth endpoint instead of a 4xx, breaking the frontend error contract and enabling error-based probing

apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx:~69: the form uses zodResolver(formSchema), but if formSchema was not extended with backupCode, zod strips it from submitted values and credentials.backupCode will always be undefined — backup-code login would be dead on arrival, silently falling through to SecondFactorRequired (P1 if confirmed; path ships untested)

EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:~282: the Download Button sits inside the Form with handleSubmit={handleEnable} without type="button" or preventDefault (unlike its sibling Copy/Close buttons), so clicking Download may also submit the form and fire a spurious enable API call with an empty TOTP code

Login 'Lost access' flow: `backupCode` is never wired into the `signIn("credentials")` call or the zod form schema in `apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx` — the rendered BackupCode input is never sent (zodResolver strips unknown keys from the unchanged formSchema), so the credentials provider takes the TOTP branch and returns `SecondFactorRequired`, which the client handles by silently re-setting `twoFactorRequired(true)` with no error shown; entering a valid backup code does nothing.

`onEnable` callback contract silently changed in `EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx`: it now fires only from the 'Close' button on the backup-codes step instead of when the enable API returns 200; dismissing via the DialogContent close (X) or Escape routes through `onOpenChange`, so the parent never learns 2FA was enabled server-side and keeps rendering the switch as off, which can lead the user to re-run setup and rotate the stored codes.

Backup-code consumption in `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:131–155` is a non-atomic read-modify-write: two concurrent sign-ins with the same code both read the pre-update snapshot and both log in (violating the single-use guarantee), and concurrent logins with different codes cause a lost update that resurrects a code the first request consumed; consumption should be atomic (e.g., conditional update or per-code comparison inside a transaction).

`MissingBackupCodes` message ('No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings.') directs users to a capability that doesn't exist — the PR adds no settings flow or endpoint to generate/regenerate backup codes for accounts with 2FA already enabled, and every user who enabled 2FA before this deploy has `backupCodes = null`, making it a dead-end instruction in an auth-recovery path.

Unvalidated `req.body.backupCode` type in `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts:~60` (same pattern at `next-auth-options.ts:~143`): a non-string value like `{"backupCode": 123}` makes `.replaceAll` throw a TypeError with no try/catch producing the documented `{ error: ErrorCode }` JSON shape, causing an unhandled 500 and breaking the client's `response.json()` error contract; validate it's a string (and trim/normalize) before use.

Shared `PasswordField` visibility toggle removed from tab order (`tabIndex={-1}` added to the show/hide button in `packages/ui/components/form/inputs/Input.tsx:47–51`): a package-wide a11y regression affecting every consumer of `@calcom/ui`'s PasswordField, since keyboard-only users can no longer reach the eye toggle; a targeted fix (e.g., autoFocus management in the specific modal) would avoid changing the contract for all callers.

`setup` endpoint (`apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts:60–61, 78`) now has a persistent side effect of generating and persisting backup codes on every call before 2FA is actually enabled: callers that abandon the flow (abandoned modal, error after password confirm, or stale cached JS during deploy) leave valid, never-displayed codes stored, and the 'lost access' path will later report them as incorrect rather than missing; consider generating codes in the `enable` endpoint instead or documenting that setup rotates them.

Non-atomic read-modify-write consumption of backup codes in authorize() (next-auth-options.ts:131-157): the entire backupCodes array is read, modified, and written back with an unconditional prisma.user.update with no transaction, version check, or conditional updateMany, so two concurrent sign-ins can both consume the same code or silently roll back consumption of a different code (last write wins), violating the single-use guarantee

backupCode may never reach the credentials provider: the zod formSchema was not updated to include backupCode, so zod strips the unknown key and values.backupCode is undefined in handleSubmit and never sent to signIn, causing the server to fall into the TOTP branch and return SecondFactorRequired with no error shown to the client, potentially making backup-code login completely non-functional

Clipboard copy in EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx (~272-281) reports success unconditionally: navigator.clipboard.writeText is fire-and-forget and the success toast runs synchronously without awaiting, so the toast appears even if the write rejects; in non-secure contexts navigator.clipboard is undefined causing a TypeError with no feedback at all

Dialog X / ESC close at the backup-codes step (EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx ~164 onOpenChange, ~261-270 close button) bypasses onEnable and resetState: the parent's 2FA switch still shows disabled even though 2FA is enabled, and the next modal open lands on the stale DisplayBackupCodes step showing the previous session's codes

Lost access flow dead-ends for pre-existing 2FA users with backupCodes = null: the login screen shows a Lost access button that can never succeed, and the 'missing_backup_codes' message tells users to generate codes in settings which they cannot do while locked out (chicken-and-egg), leaving them fully locked out with no actionable fallback

Unguarded JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(user.backupCodes, CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY)) in disable.ts (~56-58) and next-auth-options.ts (~140-142) has no try/catch: if the encryption key was rotated or the ciphertext is corrupted, it throws an opaque unhandled error (500 on the disable route, raw error out of authorize() at login) instead of returning MissingBackupCodes/InternalServerError as JSON

disable.ts (~47-50) throws new Error(ErrorCode.InternalServerError) instead of returning a JSON 500, so the client's await response.json() throws and the specific error code is lost; also inconsistent with the adjacent MissingBackupCodes branch which correctly returns res.status(400).json(...)

Object URL leak and sensitive state never cleaned up in EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx: URL.createObjectURL is revoked only when a new setup runs and resetState() (~70-74) doesn't revoke backupCodesUrl or clear backupCodes/dataUri/secret, leaking a blob URL per open-setup-close cycle and leaving plaintext backup codes plus the TOTP secret lingering in component state after the dialog closes

No input normalization on backup-code comparison: codes are generated as lowercase hex but comparison is an exact indexOf on replaceAll('-','') with no trim and no case folding, so uppercase entry (invited by the uppercase XXXXX-XXXXX placeholder) or trailing whitespace causes a correctly copied code to fail with 'Backup code is incorrect'

Non-string backupCode crashes the handler with a 500: req.body.backupCode.replaceAll(...) in disable.ts (~61-62) and credentials.backupCode in authorize() (next-auth-options.ts ~145) assume a string, so a crafted body like {"backupCode": 123} (or an array/object) throws a TypeError producing an unhandled 500 instead of a 400 validation error

No test exercises backup-code login at all: the new authorize() backup-code branch (next-auth-options.ts:130-155), the 'Lost access' UI toggle, and the signInCallback error handling are completely untested — the added e2e only covers the download filename and a toast

Potential bug: backupCode was added to LoginValues but the formSchema used by zodResolver (login.tsx:67) shows no update in the diff — if the zod schema doesn't include backupCode, the resolver strips it from submitted values, credentials.backupCode is always undefined, and backup login silently dead-ends in a SecondFactorRequired loop

Single-use consumption invariant is untested (next-auth-options.ts:147-153): no test verifies that a used backup code is rejected on reuse, so a regression allowing unlimited replay of a leaked code would ship silently

Race condition in the consume-on-use logic: the read-modify-write pattern (backupCodes[index] = null + re-encrypt) allows two concurrent logins with the same backup code to both succeed because both read the original array before either writes

Disable-2FA-with-backup-code path is untested (disable.ts:47-66, DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx:103-110): valid backup code, wrong code, and the MissingBackupCodes branch for legacy users whose backupCodes is null all have no coverage

New error copy ('Please generate them in your settings') directs users to a regenerate-backup-codes flow that doesn't exist anywhere in this diff — misleading for exactly the legacy users who will hit it

navigator.clipboard.writeText(...) is not awaited before showToast(...) fires unconditionally (EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:276-280), so the copy-success toast appears even when the copy actually fails (clipboard permissions, unfocused document, non-secure context)

The copy test asserts a toast UI signal rather than actual clipboard content (login.2fa.e2e.ts:120-121), so it passes even when copying fails — the in-test TODO ('check clipboard content') concedes this

Known false-passing assertion left as a FIXME instead of fixed in the test this PR extends (login.2fa.e2e.ts:50-53): expect(locator.isChecked()).toBeTruthy() evaluates once without retrying and passes even when the switch is not checked; the trivial fix is await expect(locator).toBeChecked()

No edge-case coverage for backup-code input normalization: the comparison backupCodes.indexOf(code.replaceAll('-', '')) is case-sensitive with no whitespace trimming while the UI placeholder is uppercase XXXXX-XXXXX, and wrong code, consumed code, uppercase/whitespace input, and corrupt encrypted payload are all untested
Unguarded JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...)) on the encrypted backup codes payload can throw an unhandled 500 on corrupt data
Download test asserts only suggestedFilename() (login.2fa.e2e.ts:113-116) and never verifies that the 10 displayed/downloaded codes match the codes persisted encrypted in the DB

Backup codes are generated and persisted at setup time before the TOTP code is ever verified (setup.ts:61-67), and any subsequent setup call overwrites previously issued codes — no test covers re-running setup invalidating codes a user already saved, or abandoned setup flows leaving orphaned codes stored

Abandoning the flow at the DisplayBackupCodes step is a one-way door (EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:200-210, 261-269): the Cancel button is hidden, closing via the dialog's X/Esc (onOpenChange) skips onEnable, and since no view/regenerate backup codes UI exists anywhere in this diff the codes can never be displayed again — untested

Backup-code verification logic is duplicated verbatim across disable.ts:46-67 and next-auth-options.ts:131-154 (encryption-key guard, symmetricDecrypt, JSON.parse, replaceAll("-",""), indexOf, error mapping) with no shared helper, making the encrypted-JSON-array storage format an implicit contract duplicated in two files; the copies already diverge in consumption semantics (login nulls one code, disable deletes all), inviting drift; a verifyBackupCode(user, input) helper should be extracted into @calcom/features/auth/lib
Misleading comment at disable.ts:66 ('if user has 2fa and NOT using backup code, try totp') sits inside the backup-code branch but describes the else-if below it
setup.ts:65 encrypts with CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY without the !process.env guard that both verification copies added

BackupCode.tsx:7 exports a component named TwoFactor (a copy-paste artifact from TwoFactor.tsx), leaving two live components named TwoFactor; the name is wrong in React DevTools, stack traces, and any grep for 'TwoFactor'

onEnable() in EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:263-271 fires only from the backup-codes Close button; dismissing via dialog X/Escape (onOpenChange) never calls onEnable, so the parent settings UI is never told 2FA was enabled and its switch desyncs from reality

resetState/resetForm are wired only into explicit buttons; onOpenChange (X/Esc) resets nothing, so reopening a modal resumes at a stale step (e.g., DisplayBackupCodes) with stale error text, and DisableTwoFactorModal's Cancel leaves twoFactorLostAccess set for the next open; reset should be centralized on dialog open/close rather than duplicated per button

resetState clears only password/errorMessage/step — backupCodes, dataUri, secret (the TOTP secret), and backupCodesUrl all survive the reset, so plaintext backup codes and the TOTP secret linger in component memory after the flow completes

The backup-code format contract (10 hex chars, dash after position 5, 10 codes) is re-encoded independently across five locations (setup.ts:61, BackupCode.tsx:22-24, EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:163, disable.ts:59, next-auth-options.ts:144) with no shared constant or format/parse helper; a missed site produces silent validation mismatches (e.g., UI accepts 11 chars, server compares 10)

backupCodesUrl is revoked only when a subsequent handleSetup overwrites it and never in resetState or on unmount (EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:95-99), so every completed setup flow leaks a blob URL containing the plaintext codes for the life of the page

Untyped state at the API boundary (EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:63): useState([]) infers never[] and body from response.json() is any, so there is no compile-time contract that setup returns backupCodes: string[]; a server response-shape change fails silently at runtime instead of at compile time; should be useState<string[]>([]) with a typed response

.replaceAll("-", "") is called directly on req.body.backupCode / credentials.backupCode (disable.ts:59, next-auth-options.ts:144) with no typeof check or schema validation; a non-string JSON value throws a TypeError and surfaces as an unhandled 500 rather than a 400

throw new Error(...) at disable.ts:47-49 for the missing-encryption-key path breaks the route's JSON error contract: Next.js turns it into a 500 HTML page while every other error path in the handler returns res.status(...).json({ error }), so the client (DisableTwoFactorModal -> response.json()) hits a JSON parse failure instead of the InternalServerError code it maps

Known-broken e2e assertion committed at login.2fa.e2e.ts:50-52: expect(page.locator(...).isChecked()).toBeTruthy() asserts on a Promise object which is always truthy, so the check can never fail (as the FIXME admits); it should use toBeChecked() instead of committing a FIXME
New backup-code e2e coverage ships with TODOs for download-file and clipboard content, leaving those behaviors untested while the suite appears to cover them

Error copy for 'missing_backup_codes' (common.json:2019) says 'Please generate them in your settings,' but the PR adds no regenerate-backup-codes UI or endpoint (codes are only created during initial setup); pre-feature 2FA users with backupCodes: null are told to perform an action they cannot do without first disabling 2FA

next-auth-options.ts:147-154: the authorize() credentials callback both verifies the backup code and burns it (DB write) before the session is actually created; if anything later in the login flow fails, the user loses a code without gaining access; consumption should be a separate post-success step

TwoFactorAuthAPI.ts:22: disable(password, code, backupCode: string) makes backupCode a required parameter even though it is empty whenever the user authenticates via TOTP; callers must pass empty values and the server relies on truthiness; it should be backupCode?: string so the type reflects the actual contract

'Lost access' toggle logic is duplicated between login.tsx:103-131 and DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx:113-121 with divergent semantics (login's 'go back' from backup mode returns to the TOTP step, creating a two-hop path back to password); a shared hook/component would keep the two copies from drifting further

Login with a backup code likely never sends `backupCode` to the server: in `apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx`, neither the submit handler's `signIn("credentials", {...})` call nor `formSchema` was updated to include `backupCode`, and since zodResolver strips keys not in the schema, the server never receives the code, throws `SecondFactorRequired`, and `handleError` just re-sets `twoFactorRequired` with no error message — the lost-access recovery flow silently no-ops when the user submits a valid backup code.

Backfill gap: the `backupCodes` column lands as NULL for every existing user, and codes are generated only in `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts`, which is reachable only when (re-)enabling 2FA — existing 2FA users have no path to generate backup codes without first disabling 2FA, which requires the TOTP they may have lost.

The `missing_backup_codes` error message tells users 'No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings,' but this PR adds no settings control to regenerate codes, dead-ending the users most likely to need backup codes with a misleading instruction.

`resetState` in `apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx` clears only `password`/`errorMessage`/`step` and never clears `backupCodes`, `backupCodesUrl`, `dataUri`, or `secret`, so stale secrets and codes persist.
`URL.revokeObjectURL` is only called when a new setup runs, so the blob object URL is never released on dialog close/unmount, causing a memory leak.

The dialog's X/ESC close path (`onOpenChange`) never calls `resetState`, so closing at the `DisplayBackupCodes` step via X skips `onEnable()` and the parent's 2FA switch state can go stale even though 2FA is now enabled server-side.

Backup code input is not normalized server-side: verification in `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts` and `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts` only does `replaceAll("-", "")` before an exact `indexOf`, so a valid code pasted with leading/trailing whitespace (likely when copying a line from the newline-joined `cal-backup-codes.txt`) or retyped in uppercase fails with 'Backup code is incorrect'; a `.trim()` and case-fold before comparison would fix it.

Backup-code consumption is not atomic (read-modify-write in `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`): the list is decrypted, the matched index nulled, and re-encrypted in a separate `prisma.user.update`, so two concurrent sign-ins presenting the same code can both pass `indexOf` before either write lands and a 'single-use' code can be consumed twice.
The backup code is persisted as burned before the sign-in is guaranteed to complete, so a later failure in the authorize chain wastes a valid code.

Backup code login from the login page likely never sends the code: `formSchema` was not updated to include `backupCode`, so zodResolver strips the field before the submit handler calls `signIn`, leaving `credentials.backupCode` undefined and causing the server to fall into the TOTP branch and return `SecondFactorRequired` with no error message — a silent no-op where submitting a valid backup code does nothing visible (apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx:43)

Non-atomic read-modify-write consumption of backup codes in next-auth-options.ts (~146-158): decrypt → indexOf → null out slot → re-encrypt → prisma.user.update has no transaction, version check, or conditional update, so two concurrent sign-ins can clobber each other's writes, resurrecting an already-used code and allowing a single code to be replayed concurrently to mint multiple sessions, violating the single-use guarantee

EnableTwoFactorModal: `onEnable()` now only fires on the 'Close' button, but the dialog remains closable via X/ESC/`onOpenChange(false)` which never calls `onEnable()` or `resetState()`, leaving the parent settings UI showing 2FA disabled while it's actually enabled, showing a stale codes grid on reopen, and cascading into data loss when the user re-runs the enable flow and setup.ts:60 unconditionally regenerates and overwrites backupCodes, silently invalidating codes the user already saved

No regeneration path for existing 2FA users: users who enabled 2FA before this feature have `backupCodes = null`, and the 'missing_backup_codes' error message directs them to generate codes in settings, but no settings UI or endpoint exists to generate codes while 2FA is enabled (codes are only created in setup.ts via the enable flow, which flips twoFactorEnabled false and rotates the secret), so the only way to obtain codes is to disable 2FA first — requiring the TOTP code the user may have lost

Known-broken e2e assertion shipped in login.2fa.e2e.ts:50-53: `isChecked()` returns a Promise and Playwright's generic `toBeTruthy()` does not await it, so the assertion always passes whether or not the 2FA switch is checked — the only guard verifying 2FA enablement in the flow is a silent pass; fix with `await expect(locator).toBeChecked()`

Backup code comparison is case-sensitive: codes are generated as lowercase hex but compared via strict `indexOf` after only stripping dashes, so a user who types a code with uppercase A-F gets a false 'incorrect backup code' rejection at the moment they may be locked out; normalize with `.toLowerCase()` before comparing (next-auth-options.ts ~146, disable.ts ~60)

'Copied!' toast is shown even when the clipboard write fails: `navigator.clipboard.writeText` is fire-and-forget (not awaited, no `.catch`) and the success toast runs unconditionally, so on insecure contexts, denied clipboard permission, or non-focused documents the write rejects unhandled while the user is falsely told the codes were copied (EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx ~272-281)

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx` a new `backupCode` field is added to `LoginValues` and the UI conditionally renders `<BackupCode />`, which registers `backupCode` via `useFormContext()`. adjudication_records.issue_text: Non-atomic read-modify-write consumption of backup codes in next-auth-options.ts (~146-158): decrypt → indexOf → null out slot → re-encrypt → prisma.user.update has no transaction, version check, or conditional update, so two concurrent sign-ins can clobber each other's writes, resurrecting an already-used code and allowing a single code to be replayed concurrently to mint multiple sessions, violating the single-use guarantee

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, backup-code consumption is implemented as a read-modify-write sequence: decrypt stored `user.backupCodes` → `indexOf(credentials.backupCode...)` → set `backupCodes[index] = null` → `prisma.user.update(...)` with the re-encrypted array. There is no transaction, conditional update, or optimistic concurrency check tying the update to the previously read value. Two concurrent sign-ins using the same backup code can both pass the `indexOf` check before either write commits, resulting in the same backup code being accepted twice (minting multiple sessions), which violates the intended single-use property.
